questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been to The Netherlands several times, mainly Amsterdam, and I genuinely enjoy spending time there. Therefore, I chose to go to Rotterdam to experience more of the country. Moreover, Erasmus School of Law is well recognized within the field of company/commercial law + European law.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Comparable to UCPH. Of course, considering I only followed MA-courses although I am a BA-student at UCPH, the complexity of the courses were a bit higher.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching methods were completely different from what I am used to from UCPH. A lot more student-involvement, including us students collecting material for our assignments etc., was a huge part of the teaching. This both made the education feel more academic bu at the same time less structured.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Blok 1: Research & Writing Skills - Company and Commercial Law (15 ECTS). 
Blok 2: Mediation Advocacy - Theory and Practice (5 ECTS) and Law and Policy of European Integration (10 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of the three mentioned. 

The course in Blok 1 had a very student-involving way of teaching. It consisted of a lot of assignment, where we as students had to find the material ourselves to be able to answer the assignments. The course is meant to make the student more able to conduct and write their MA-thesis in the end of the master. This makes the course very flexible and highly academic. 

The courses in second blok are quite similar to the way courses in law are tought at UCPH. In Law and Policy of European Integration, we had to write three assignments that counts 40 % of our final grade in the course as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely go to cities surrounding the city you live in. I went to Amsterdam, Den Haag, Antwerp, Brussels, Delft, Eindhoven, Utrecht etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Approach them in the student café; go on dates; be openminded.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Actually none. As long as you act respectful towards others and ask openly about their culture heritage, then it should be fine.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The direct- and openness; not being afraid to ask questions too directly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Build up a professional relationship with the professors! Many of them are well-recognized academic people which can be in your favor in the long run. 
2) If you have physical classes, go to as many as possible to be able to socialize with other students. Then you have someone to have a coffee with, discuss an assignment with etc. 
3) Be open and ask questions - no questions are dumb questions. It can be challenging to conduct knowledge on another language than the one of your mother-tongue. The more you ask, the more effectively can you perform.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being more self-aware of my capabilities.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking English - both in a social and a legal context.
